title: behERZt - Physical activity-related health promotion for older people in rural communities in the districts of ore mountains
summary:
In structurally weak regions such as the ore mountains, there is often a deficit with regard to the provision of needs-based exercise programs as a measure to promote health and strengthen social cohesion for the particularly strongly represented population group of older people aged 65 and over. By increasing the density of offers in the area of exercise promotion, accessibility for older people in rural areas can be improved so that as many older people as possible can benefit from the proven positive biopsychosocial health effects of regular and communal exercise activities. The “behERZt” project aims to implement health-promoting (evidence-based) exercise programs in communities in the ore mountains for older people (aged 65 and over), some of whom live alone. This involves promoting motor skills (strength, endurance, coordination, mobility) and everyday cognitive functions (e.g. memory, attention, mental flexibility) on a needs-specific and group-based basis. The health-promoting interventions and supervision of the exercise groups are carried out by exercise instructors and exercise mentors.
In addition to implementing the physical activity offers, local actors and organizations from different sectors and social institutions (e.g. mayors, sports clubs, citizens' meeting, physicians) are networked with each other in order to anchor the health promotion measures in the area of physical and social activity structurally and thus sustainably in the municipalities. The project contributes to improving exercise-related healthcare and promotes equal health opportunities and social cohesion among older people in rural areas. At the same time, it supports the goal of “healthy ageing” pursued in the ore mountain district.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•  Independent travel to the location of the exercise programme (green and park areas of the respective district)
•  Basic knowledge of the German language
Exclusion criteria:
• There is a medical prohibition against physical exertion.
• A serious, medically diagnosed health event within the last 6 months (e.g. heart attack, stroke, bone fractures, operations, pneumonia).
•  Diagnosed dementia or major depression
•  Participation in other clinical trials, e.g. to test new drugs
